scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “Uniform computation of the squared-logarithmic k-server bound” (preprints/Uniform-computation-of-the-squared-logarithmic-k-server-bound-September-24-2026/Uniform-computation-of-the-squared-logarithmic-k-server-bound-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 110 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 2e665c0419f62ed4), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 1. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are an absolute constant C and a polynomial p with the following property. Let n ≥ 3, 2 ≤ k < n, let d be a rational metric on X = {1, . . . , n}, and let s ∈ Xk be an initial labeled tuple, with repetitions allowed. Write L for the total binary encoding length of n, k, d, s. A single uniform randomized online algorithm preprocesses these data in at most p(L) bit operations and serves request rt, for every reachable history and internal state, in at most p(L + ⌈log2(t + 1)⌉) additional bit operations. It uses only unbiased random bits and moves exactly one chosen server to each request, permitting a zero-length move. For every fixed finite request sequence σ independent of those bits, E costA,s(σ) ≤ C log(k + 1) 2 OPTs(σ) + Bd,k,s, (1) where Bd,k,s is finite and independent of σ and its length. The algorithm does not need to know that length in advance.
